dedupe_keys.name: shake table test of a resilient full scale ten story mass timber building

description: Shake Table Test of a Resilient Full-Scale Ten-Story Mass Timber Building is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Shiling Pei, Colorado School of Mines (mines.edu). A test program was designed to answer if it is possible to design and build a tall mass timber building with resilient performance against large earthquakes. Resilient performance was defined as to receive no structural damage under design level earthquake, and only easily repairable damage under maximum considered earthquake. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 5 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-sxq1-p731. Keywords: Mass timber, resilience, shake table test, rocking wall, tall wood building. Published 2024-11-15. Facility named: Six Degree of Freedom Large High-Performance Outdoor Shake Table (LHPOST6) - University of California, San Diego. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
